raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation
The LoRA tests had grown into a matrix of model runs, second-backend arms, loud startup validators and shape snapshots that cost per-PR GPU time without guarding anything a silent failure could slip through, and there was no single command to run them. This PR applies one rule to every LoRA test — a test stays in per-PR CI only if its removal could let a silent failure through (wrong weights, routing, slot or graph buffer with no error); matrices, second-backend arms, perf and loud startup checks move to the nightly or weekly suites, duplicates go — and adds a `lora` rerun group so a LoRA change can be validated with `/run-cpu-ci` + `/rerun-group lora`. Since LoRA code changes are rare, the per-PR tier keeps only four GPU canaries plus the CPU units and the path-gated kernel lane; every other LoRA GPU test runs through the nightly suites, whose schedule fires about every other day (`0 14 */2 * *`), so a regression from an unrelated PR shows up on the next nightly run that completes, not before merge. Main's CUDA re-tier (#47619) put the LoRA e2e tests in extra and the gpt-oss-20b case in weekly; this PR takes the LoRA e2e tests one tier further (nightly), keeps `test_lora_tp` per PR as a 2-GPU canary, and leaves the gpt-oss-20b case in weekly. The numbers below are registered seconds (GPU-weighted where noted), not PR wall time or cost.

By registration (`est_time` summed over the LoRA tests, weighted by the runner's GPU count; the same files on main at their old paths):

| Tier | main (106 files, at b80178734d) | this PR (112 files) |
|---|---|---|
| per PR (including the path-gated kernel lane) | 3,103 s registered / 2,861 GPU-weighted, 76 registrations | 1,642 s / 1,948, 75 registrations |
| extra (label-gated, also main twice a day) | 2,070 s / 4,709, 14 | none |
| nightly (main every two days) | 584 s / 1,301, 6 | 2,997 s / 4,714, 30 |
| weekly | 2,712 s / 18,518, 9 | 2,562 s / 18,338, 11 |

(The 112 files are the LoRA tests this PR touches or groups: the 110 members of the `lora` rerun group plus the two weekly 8×B200 giant-model tests it leaves out; 17 of them are tests outside the LoRA directories with LoRA-named cases, unchanged by this PR, so they add the same time to both columns.)

Per-PR LoRA registered GPU-seconds drop by a third (2,861 → 1,948) on top of #47619, which had already moved four LoRA e2e tests from the per-PR tier to extra and the gpt-oss-20b case to weekly; 1,188 of the remaining 1,948 is the kernel-unit lane, which runs only on PRs that touch kernel paths and on main's scheduled runs (twice a day). What runs on every PR is the MoE LoRA engine under prefill and decode graphs (`csgmv` and `triton_v2`, compared with the same engine run eagerly), multi-adapter dense batches on the default `csgmv` backend compared with HF row by row (`torch_native` attention, graphs and radix cache off, no overlap loading), LoRA with EAGLE, LoRA at TP=2, and four small 5090 units; the kernel lane gained witnesses for the FP8 MoE runner under graph replay and the Blackwell execution of the MoE runner numerics. Graph-versus-eager comparisons are not an independent model reference: a loading or scaling error shared by both paths would pass them, and the independent MoE reference (the vLLM parity test) now runs nightly.

## Commits (eight, rebased on main, meant to be read in order)

1. **`test: consolidate the LoRA CPU unit tests`** — `test_mem_pool_ep_unit` 49 → 13 tests plus a rank-tail guard (a smaller-rank MoE adapter reusing a slot must clear the larger adapter's tail rows); `test_eviction_policy` keeps the candidate-set guard; UNO fast-path and auto-detect tests move into the DP-attention and init-modules files; loud validators, shape snapshots and the Laguna dims move to weekly CPU (`test_lora_startup_contracts`, `test_mem_pool_layouts`); four duplicate units removed; GPU-free kernel checks become CPU units (`test_moe_lora_provider_contract`, `test_moe_lora_contiguous_bounds`); lifecycle guards that need no server become CPU units (`test_lora_overlap_loader_unit`, `unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_lora_path`, `unit/managers/test_lora_lru_unload_unit`, which also checks that an unload waits for every request still holding the adapter); `lora/test_lora_drainer` is removed (main's `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer` from #46500 covers the drainer's admission logic on the CPU suite; the file's remaining server run only checked batch splitting under a drain through `run_lora_batch_splitting_equivalence_test`, which commit 3 replaces); `test_lora_openai_api` gains a `base-a-test-cpu` registration (it was only on the Intel CPU suite).
2. **`test: reorganize the LoRA kernel tests into per-PR witnesses and extra matrices`** — `test_fused_moe_lora_kernel` (108 → 6 cases on the production tiles) and `test_virtual_experts_kernels` move under `kernels/ops/lora` (`pr-test-xpu.yml` follows); three wide files keep one independent witness per execution path per PR and send their matrices to extra-a with shared fixtures in `sglang.test.kits.inkling_sink_lora_kit` / `moe_lora_down_b_kit`; `test_virtual_experts_kernels` keeps the sentinel/remap checks and an exact-placement align check on both align paths, while main's capacity, staged-routing and graph-replay matrices live in `test_virtual_experts_kernels_matrix` on extra-a; new per-PR guards: the FP8 MoE runner under graph replay, production-launch fused-MoE cases and align completeness, three SM100-only dense plan combinations, Inkling QKVR and padded lm_head slicing in `test_linear_parallel_groups`; the Marlin direct-decode inactive-route case moves from the generic Marlin matrix into `unit/lora/test_experimental_sgl_marlin_shared_outer_reduce` (extra-a, 5090) so the `lora` group reaches it; the MoE runner numerics get a second registration on the existing `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` job; `est_time` calibrated from the `/rerun-group lora` run on c80c0a00e9 (1.5× measured, minimum 10 s), main's values kept where its newer cases arrived later, and re-measured in the 2026-10-30 reruns for the files that ran longer than their estimate (nine files raised; none lowered on a single warm run).
3. **`test: share the LoRA accuracy references and comparisons through sglang.test.lora_utils`** — one trainer-reference comparison for the eight `*_logprob_diff` files (nonempty, finite, exactly the recorded length), the MoE vLLM reference data and TP generation, and `assert_lora_routes_match_hf` for overlap-loaded and multi-adapter batches (split and mixed, one server); the HF comparison keeps the chunked guard on the harness default backend as a direct SGLang → HF comparison; the vLLM parity test gains a virtual-experts arm with its own measured bounds; MoE TP runs once at TP=2 on 2-gpu-large (the chunked-logprob case in its own extra-a file); `test_lora_tp` runs per PR (base-b) on 2-gpu-large instead of extra-b on 8×H200, where #47619 had put it, with the overlap arm as its own extra-a file; Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3-VL keep the extra-b stage from #47619, Qwen3-VL at TP=2 on 2-gpu-large.
4. **`test: merge the LoRA lifecycle e2e tests and fail closed in the graph guards`** — `test_lora_update` is one merged case on two launches (1,558 → 431 lines: eviction pressure by construction, a q,v-only adapter reusing an all-module slot, adapter-name reuse, `/v1/models`, a never-evicting static reference; `test_lora_eviction` folds into it); the MoE prefill-graph matrix is split over `sglang.test.kits.lora_prefill_graph_kit` into a per-PR slice and an extra file, and the kit fails closed (two graph prefills and decode-graph replays with no eager fallback, read from `/metrics`; every decode row's top-5 compared with eager decode on a shared prefix); with #46720's fix in, the `triton_v2` arms run with the dual (lora/nolora) decode graph enabled, decode the decode prompts mixed → base-only → mixed at batch size 4, and record the replayed (batch size, variant) keys in the scheduler through the Engine's `run_scheduler_process_func` override, so each batch must show its own variant's replay in its own request window; the BCG lone-request log probe is the replay evidence (the whole-log check it subsumed is gone); the legacy-Triton BCG arm is a thin extra-a entry point over `sglang.test.kits.bcg_lora_kit`; spec decoding runs real EAGLE models with a graph limit checked through the counters; disaggregation outputs drop to 32 tokens; the RL tensor-load test moves to the 5090 lane.
5. **`test: widen the decode tolerance of the RuterNorway LoRA case to 0.3`** — `test_lora_tp_overlap_loading` fails on 2×H100 at one decode position where HF fp16 generate and SGLang fp16 TP2 differ by 0.140 against the 0.1 bound. Against an fp32 HF+PEFT reference, HF fp16 deviates by about +0.080 and SGLang by about −0.060 at that token; without the adapter every pipeline is within 0.03. This adapter's LoRA deltas are as large as the base q/v projections (delta/base RMS up to 1.68), so fp16 tail logprobs move with the execution path (GPU, TP, CUDA graph vs eager, attention kernel), while overlap loading and the LoRA backends change nothing; main's own `test_lora_tp.py` overlap arm fails identically on 2×H100. 0.3 covers the observed paths (a measured TP1 path would be about 0.234) and still rejects a dropped adapter (2.1–8.4 nats at that position). Only `run_lora_test_one_by_one` reads the per-adaptor decode tolerance.
6. **`ci: add a lora /rerun-group group`** — every test whose subject is LoRA across all tiers: the LoRA directories (including main's new `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer` and `unit/lora/test_lora_pp`), the LoRA tests parked elsewhere, and the registered tests with a LoRA-named case (adapter counters, `lora_path` normalization, LoRA slots in scheduling, the LoRA name table and KV-event adapter names, `LoRARef` serialization, LoRA forward domains, the deferred all-reduce under LoRA, the LoRA gate/up wrapper in the fused dual GEMM, weight reload through `FusedMoEWithLoRA`, the Inkling LoRA layout, model LoRA hooks, the `after_down` hook, the LoRA top-k unpack): 110 members, 114 runs across 6 pools (files with an H100 and a B200 registration run on both). The commit message lists what stays out and why: the two weekly 8×B200 giant-model tests (DeepSeek-V3.1-Base, 1,800 s, and Kimi-K2.5, 420 s, which would add an 8-GPU Blackwell job to every routine rerun; they keep their weekly registrations and run one at a time with `/rerun-test`), the 720 s generic Marlin matrix, the 480 s UNO e2e, AMD-only and Intel-only registrations, diffusion LoRA, manual tests, incidental mentions.
7. **`ci: keep four LoRA canaries per PR and move the other LoRA GPU tests to nightly`** — per PR: `test_lora_moe_prefill_cuda_graph`, `test_multi_lora_backend`, `test_lora_spec_decoding`, `test_lora_tp` and four 5090 units (under a minute together); the other 24 per-PR and extra LoRA GPU registrations become `stage="nightly"` on their pool with `est_time` and `runner_config` kept (the five 5090 files stay on `1-gpu-small`, a row the nightly workflow has had since #47619); the gpt-oss-20b case stays in weekly, and the Nemotron-120B and LoRA-latency cases were already nightly on main after #47619; the moved files' docstrings and comments say nightly. Ordinary per-PR LoRA registrations outside the kernel-unit lane go from 1,416 to 760 GPU-weighted seconds, extra from 2,757 GPU-seconds (every labelled PR and twice a day on main) to none; per run the nightly suites gain 1,387 registered seconds on H100, 246 on the 5090, 670 on 2×H100 (1,340 GPU-weighted) and 110 on 4×H100 (440 GPU-weighted), and 4×B200 is unchanged. What a non-LoRA PR can now break without failing its own CI, found only on the next completed nightly run: adapter lifecycle and eviction, HiCache adapter isolation, the independent MoE reference (vLLM parity), overlap loading, PD transfer, the dense breakable prefill graph, the chunked-prefill HF guard, RL tensor loading and the TP matrices.
8. **`test: retry the adapter download in test_lora_load_from_tensor on hub rate limits`** — the 5090 batch of the group rerun on this branch failed in this file's `setUpClass` on a hub 429 ("3000 api requests per 5 minutes", retry after 49 s) with no cached adapter on the runner; CI retries test methods, not `setUpClass`, and waits about two seconds. The adapter download now goes through `sglang.srt.utils.retry` (three retries, about 30, 60 and 60 s).
Rerun convention (a review rule, not path-based CI enforcement): a PR that changes `python/sglang/srt/lora`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora` or the LoRA tests runs `/rerun-group lora` before merge; a PR that changes the scheduler, the radix or HiCache caches, PD disaggregation or model LoRA integration reruns the affected LoRA tests with `/rerun-test`.

## Validation
- `/rerun-group lora` on an earlier head of this branch (c80c0a00e9): 92 members, 96 runs across 7 pools, all green. On review that run carried one failure hidden by the test framework's automatic CI retry (the TP-overlap mismatch above); read every attempt, not only job status.
- Targeted CI on 3ba65fbd8c (the same content as this head before the rebases, minus the tolerance commit): the six CPU files and the Marlin runtime unit (ubuntu), both virtual-experts files, the parallel-groups test, the Marlin shared-outer unit and the RL test (5090), the six H100 kernel files plus the routing test (H100), the MoE runner numerics (B200), vLLM parity, spec decoding, multi-LoRA, overlap loading and the Qwen3-8B trainer comparison (H100), TP, MoE TP and TP overlap loading (2×H100): all passed with no retried attempt, except the two items below. The tolerance commit then passed `test_lora_tp_overlap_loading` on 2×H100 on its first attempt.
- **Decode-graph fault, now fixed on main:** the per-PR prefill-graph file failed Guard C on H100 (both attempts) and on H200 on a production fault — the `triton_v2` + `lora_cutedsl` decode graph gave one adapter row a wrong token after graph prefills (the full-graph arm failed the same way on GB300). The guard is correct and stays as written; #46720 (merged 2026-10-30) fixed the attention-metadata lifetime across graph variants, and this head is rebased onto it. With the dual decode graph enabled in the `triton_v2` arms and the replay observer (commit 4), both prefill-graph files pass on a GB300 (SM103, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2) at this tree on their first attempt, 75 s and 128 s, so the original Blackwell failure is closed on the hardware where it reproduced; on this head the pair also passed on H100 (run 41144682705: 102 s and 155 s, no retry) and on B200 (run 41144657118: 206 s and 130 s, no retry).
- Before CI, every file that does not need gated Llama weights was run on an H200 at the exact tree (CPU units, 10 kernel files, parity, Qwen3-8B, MoE TP2, both prefill-graph files, HiCache); earlier rounds on a GB300.
- `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` over every registered test, pre-commit over every file this PR touches, and the handler's own `resolve_test_group_specs("lora")` are green at this head. This head is a rebase onto main 8ecabd3c1e and a re-split of the validated commits. Main's LoRA changes since the validated runs and how they are absorbed: #46500 rewrote `LoRADrainer` and moved its unit tests to `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer.py` — this PR's own drainer unit (written against the old API) is dropped in favour of main's file, which joins the `lora` group unchanged; #45951 (multi-LoRA under PP) added `unit/lora/test_lora_pp.py`, which joins the group unchanged, and three constructor arguments of `LoRAMemoryPool`, taken over in `test_mem_pool_ep_unit`; #46743 added a csgmv segment-grid case to `test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph`, merged as is; #46720 changed only `test_lora_inactive_batch_skip`, a group member this PR does not touch; three one-line AMD suite renames and the bot's `est_time` refresh in #46481 (the refreshed values are taken for the files whose estimates this PR does not set, and this PR's calibrated values are kept for the 17 files it re-estimated, moved or deleted). On top, a test-only simplification is folded into the four test commits (seven single-use helpers inlined, the in-place MoE fixture specialized to its one call, docstrings and comments shortened; 15 of the 22 touched files are identical to the validated content once docstrings are stripped, and the other 7 change only how a local helper is called; test cases, assertions, registrations, hardware placement, `est_time` and tolerances are unchanged). The tree was not rerun through CI as such.

- Folded into the six commits on 2026-10-30 after review: the group completion, the Marlin relocation, the dual-graph decode arms with the replay observer, the overlap-loader immediate-completion guard and the fixture simplifications. Checked per commit (compile, registered-test lint, import resolution), pre-commit on every touched file, the handler's `resolve_test_group_specs("lora")` (110 members, 114 runs, 6 pools, no error), CPU runs of the touched CPU files; the down-B kit's plans and launch config compared before and after on CPU are identical. `/rerun-group lora` on 85e8dcd0b6 (2026-10-30): 2×H100 run 41141215587, 4×B200 41141230720, 5090 41141244950 (including the relocated Marlin case), CPU 41141259062 and 4×H100 41141271618 all green; H100 run 41141200668 green on 43 of 45 files, the two prefill-graph files failing on a test-only bug in the replay observer (`sglang.Engine` is a lazy-import proxy, so the scheduler-launch override never reached the real class and the replay list stayed empty while the pass counters showed every decode step on a graph), fixed since in commit 4; the Marlin matrix (41141209927) green. The CPU suite run (41141214137) failed only on `unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py`, broken on main at that base by #47415 and fixed by #47537; this head is rebased past the fix. On d717545832 (this content before the est_time refresh): the prefill-graph pair green on H100 (41144682705) and B200 (41144657118), and the CPU suite green in every partition (41144691829). The est_time refresh and the nightly move after that are registration and comment changes only (`check_registered_tests` and the handler's group resolution pass); the rebase onto 01fde5cb62 absorbed #47603, which had removed the CI-skipped TP1-vs-TP2 case this PR had already replaced. The rebase onto b80178734d (2026-11-01) absorbed #47619, the CUDA re-tier, whose one-word stage changes conflicted in six LoRA files: this PR keeps its own stages for five of them (nightly for `test_lora_update`, `test_disaggregation_lora`, Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3-VL; per PR for the TP=2 `test_lora_tp`) and takes #47619's weekly for gpt-oss-20b; the five files this PR had moved from the 5090 to H100 return to the 5090 (`1-gpu-small`), which the nightly workflow now has, with the `est_time` they carried there (their content is what the 5090 group run 41141244950 passed, apart from one docstring; their H100 run 41242333752 at the previous head also passed). The seven commits were rebuilt from the resolved tree and checked per commit (compile, registered-test lint, import resolution); pre-commit and the handler's group resolution (110 members, 114 runs, 6 pools) pass. Main's 23 new commits touch no LoRA code but change the scheduler and both CUDA-graph runners, so `/rerun-group lora` was run on the rebased head 771658f03b (2026-11-01): H100 run 41285414398 (45 files in two partitions, 930 s and 905 s, every file on its first attempt), 2×H100 41285423494, 4×B200 41285432643, 4×H100 41285462530 and CPU 41285453071 all green; the 5090 run 41285442415 passed 12 of 13 files and errored on `rl/test_lora_load_from_tensor` before any test ran (the hub rate limit above, commit 8), after which that file passed on the 5090 at this head (run 41288518365, 2 tests, 42 s, no retry needed).

Known watch item: `test_multi_lora_backend` HF-compares the split-batch route patterns `[A,None,B]` and `[None,B,None]`, which the harness had commented out as flaky when the tolerance was exact (now ROUGE-L ≥ 0.9 on one fixed prompt). It passed in every run so far; if it flakes later, diagnose before touching the cases.

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [CI] lora: Simplify LoRA tests and add a lora rerun group

detail.body:
## Motivation
The LoRA tests had grown into a matrix of model runs, second-backend arms, loud startup validators and shape snapshots that cost per-PR GPU time without guarding anything a silent failure could slip through, and there was no single command to run them. This PR applies one rule to every LoRA test — a test stays in per-PR CI only if its removal could let a silent failure through (wrong weights, routing, slot or graph buffer with no error); matrices, second-backend arms, perf and loud startup checks move to the nightly or weekly suites, duplicates go — and adds a `lora` rerun group so a LoRA change can be validated with `/run-cpu-ci` + `/rerun-group lora`. Since LoRA code changes are rare, the per-PR tier keeps only four GPU canaries plus the CPU units and the path-gated kernel lane; every other LoRA GPU test runs through the nightly suites, whose schedule fires about every other day (`0 14 */2 * *`), so a regression from an unrelated PR shows up on the next nightly run that completes, not before merge. Main's CUDA re-tier (#47619) put the LoRA e2e tests in extra and the gpt-oss-20b case in weekly; this PR takes the LoRA e2e tests one tier further (nightly), keeps `test_lora_tp` per PR as a 2-GPU canary, and leaves the gpt-oss-20b case in weekly. The numbers below are registered seconds (GPU-weighted where noted), not PR wall time or cost.

By registration (`est_time` summed over the LoRA tests, weighted by the runner's GPU count; the same files on main at their old paths):

| Tier | main (106 files, at b80178734d) | this PR (112 files) |
|---|---|---|
| per PR (including the path-gated kernel lane) | 3,103 s registered / 2,861 GPU-weighted, 76 registrations | 1,642 s / 1,948, 75 registrations |
| extra (label-gated, also main twice a day) | 2,070 s / 4,709, 14 | none |
| nightly (main every two days) | 584 s / 1,301, 6 | 2,997 s / 4,714, 30 |
| weekly | 2,712 s / 18,518, 9 | 2,562 s / 18,338, 11 |

(The 112 files are the LoRA tests this PR touches or groups: the 110 members of the `lora` rerun group plus the two weekly 8×B200 giant-model tests it leaves out; 17 of them are tests outside the LoRA directories with LoRA-named cases, unchanged by this PR, so they add the same time to both columns.)

Per-PR LoRA registered GPU-seconds drop by a third (2,861 → 1,948) on top of #47619, which had already moved four LoRA e2e tests from the per-PR tier to extra and the gpt-oss-20b case to weekly; 1,188 of the remaining 1,948 is the kernel-unit lane, which runs only on PRs that touch kernel paths and on main's scheduled runs (twice a day). What runs on every PR is the MoE LoRA engine under prefill and decode graphs (`csgmv` and `triton_v2`, compared with the same engine run eagerly), multi-adapter dense batches on the default `csgmv` backend compared with HF row by row (`torch_native` attention, graphs and radix cache off, no overlap loading), LoRA with EAGLE, LoRA at TP=2, and four small 5090 units; the kernel lane gained witnesses for the FP8 MoE runner under graph replay and the Blackwell execution of the MoE runner numerics. Graph-versus-eager comparisons are not an independent model reference: a loading or scaling error shared by both paths would pass them, and the independent MoE reference (the vLLM parity test) now runs nightly.

## Commits (eight, rebased on main, meant to be read in order)

1. **`test: consolidate the LoRA CPU unit tests`** — `test_mem_pool_ep_unit` 49 → 13 tests plus a rank-tail guard (a smaller-rank MoE adapter reusing a slot must clear the larger adapter's tail rows); `test_eviction_policy` keeps the candidate-set guard; UNO fast-path and auto-detect tests move into the DP-attention and init-modules files; loud validators, shape snapshots and the Laguna dims move to weekly CPU (`test_lora_startup_contracts`, `test_mem_pool_layouts`); four duplicate units removed; GPU-free kernel checks become CPU units (`test_moe_lora_provider_contract`, `test_moe_lora_contiguous_bounds`); lifecycle guards that need no server become CPU units (`test_lora_overlap_loader_unit`, `unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_lora_path`, `unit/managers/test_lora_lru_unload_unit`, which also checks that an unload waits for every request still holding the adapter); `lora/test_lora_drainer` is removed (main's `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer` from #46500 covers the drainer's admission logic on the CPU suite; the file's remaining server run only checked batch splitting under a drain through `run_lora_batch_splitting_equivalence_test`, which commit 3 replaces); `test_lora_openai_api` gains a `base-a-test-cpu` registration (it was only on the Intel CPU suite).
2. **`test: reorganize the LoRA kernel tests into per-PR witnesses and extra matrices`** — `test_fused_moe_lora_kernel` (108 → 6 cases on the production tiles) and `test_virtual_experts_kernels` move under `kernels/ops/lora` (`pr-test-xpu.yml` follows); three wide files keep one independent witness per execution path per PR and send their matrices to extra-a with shared fixtures in `sglang.test.kits.inkling_sink_lora_kit` / `moe_lora_down_b_kit`; `test_virtual_experts_kernels` keeps the sentinel/remap checks and an exact-placement align check on both align paths, while main's capacity, staged-routing and graph-replay matrices live in `test_virtual_experts_kernels_matrix` on extra-a; new per-PR guards: the FP8 MoE runner under graph replay, production-launch fused-MoE cases and align completeness, three SM100-only dense plan combinations, Inkling QKVR and padded lm_head slicing in `test_linear_parallel_groups`; the Marlin direct-decode inactive-route case moves from the generic Marlin matrix into `unit/lora/test_experimental_sgl_marlin_shared_outer_reduce` (extra-a, 5090) so the `lora` group reaches it; the MoE runner numerics get a second registration on the existing `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` job; `est_time` calibrated from the `/rerun-group lora` run on c80c0a00e9 (1.5× measured, minimum 10 s), main's values kept where its newer cases arrived later, and re-measured in the 2026-10-30 reruns for the files that ran longer than their estimate (nine files raised; none lowered on a single warm run).
3. **`test: share the LoRA accuracy references and comparisons through sglang.test.lora_utils`** — one trainer-reference comparison for the eight `*_logprob_diff` files (nonempty, finite, exactly the recorded length), the MoE vLLM reference data and TP generation, and `assert_lora_routes_match_hf` for overlap-loaded and multi-adapter batches (split and mixed, one server); the HF comparison keeps the chunked guard on the harness default backend as a direct SGLang → HF comparison; the vLLM parity test gains a virtual-experts arm with its own measured bounds; MoE TP runs once at TP=2 on 2-gpu-large (the chunked-logprob case in its own extra-a file); `test_lora_tp` runs per PR (base-b) on 2-gpu-large instead of extra-b on 8×H200, where #47619 had put it, with the overlap arm as its own extra-a file; Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3-VL keep the extra-b stage from #47619, Qwen3-VL at TP=2 on 2-gpu-large.
4. **`test: merge the LoRA lifecycle e2e tests and fail closed in the graph guards`** — `test_lora_update` is one merged case on two launches (1,558 → 431 lines: eviction pressure by construction, a q,v-only adapter reusing an all-module slot, adapter-name reuse, `/v1/models`, a never-evicting static reference; `test_lora_eviction` folds into it); the MoE prefill-graph matrix is split over `sglang.test.kits.lora_prefill_graph_kit` into a per-PR slice and an extra file, and the kit fails closed (two graph prefills and decode-graph replays with no eager fallback, read from `/metrics`; every decode row's top-5 compared with eager decode on a shared prefix); with #46720's fix in, the `triton_v2` arms run with the dual (lora/nolora) decode graph enabled, decode the decode prompts mixed → base-only → mixed at batch size 4, and record the replayed (batch size, variant) keys in the scheduler through the Engine's `run_scheduler_process_func` override, so each batch must show its own variant's replay in its own request window; the BCG lone-request log probe is the replay evidence (the whole-log check it subsumed is gone); the legacy-Triton BCG arm is a thin extra-a entry point over `sglang.test.kits.bcg_lora_kit`; spec decoding runs real EAGLE models with a graph limit checked through the counters; disaggregation outputs drop to 32 tokens; the RL tensor-load test moves to the 5090 lane.
5. **`test: widen the decode tolerance of the RuterNorway LoRA case to 0.3`** — `test_lora_tp_overlap_loading` fails on 2×H100 at one decode position where HF fp16 generate and SGLang fp16 TP2 differ by 0.140 against the 0.1 bound. Against an fp32 HF+PEFT reference, HF fp16 deviates by about +0.080 and SGLang by about −0.060 at that token; without the adapter every pipeline is within 0.03. This adapter's LoRA deltas are as large as the base q/v projections (delta/base RMS up to 1.68), so fp16 tail logprobs move with the execution path (GPU, TP, CUDA graph vs eager, attention kernel), while overlap loading and the LoRA backends change nothing; main's own `test_lora_tp.py` overlap arm fails identically on 2×H100. 0.3 covers the observed paths (a measured TP1 path would be about 0.234) and still rejects a dropped adapter (2.1–8.4 nats at that position). Only `run_lora_test_one_by_one` reads the per-adaptor decode tolerance.
6. **`ci: add a lora /rerun-group group`** — every test whose subject is LoRA across all tiers: the LoRA directories (including main's new `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer` and `unit/lora/test_lora_pp`), the LoRA tests parked elsewhere, and the registered tests with a LoRA-named case (adapter counters, `lora_path` normalization, LoRA slots in scheduling, the LoRA name table and KV-event adapter names, `LoRARef` serialization, LoRA forward domains, the deferred all-reduce under LoRA, the LoRA gate/up wrapper in the fused dual GEMM, weight reload through `FusedMoEWithLoRA`, the Inkling LoRA layout, model LoRA hooks, the `after_down` hook, the LoRA top-k unpack): 110 members, 114 runs across 6 pools (files with an H100 and a B200 registration run on both). The commit message lists what stays out and why: the two weekly 8×B200 giant-model tests (DeepSeek-V3.1-Base, 1,800 s, and Kimi-K2.5, 420 s, which would add an 8-GPU Blackwell job to every routine rerun; they keep their weekly registrations and run one at a time with `/rerun-test`), the 720 s generic Marlin matrix, the 480 s UNO e2e, AMD-only and Intel-only registrations, diffusion LoRA, manual tests, incidental mentions.
7. **`ci: keep four LoRA canaries per PR and move the other LoRA GPU tests to nightly`** — per PR: `test_lora_moe_prefill_cuda_graph`, `test_multi_lora_backend`, `test_lora_spec_decoding`, `test_lora_tp` and four 5090 units (under a minute together); the other 24 per-PR and extra LoRA GPU registrations become `stage="nightly"` on their pool with `est_time` and `runner_config` kept (the five 5090 files stay on `1-gpu-small`, a row the nightly workflow has had since #47619); the gpt-oss-20b case stays in weekly, and the Nemotron-120B and LoRA-latency cases were already nightly on main after #47619; the moved files' docstrings and comments say nightly. Ordinary per-PR LoRA registrations outside the kernel-unit lane go from 1,416 to 760 GPU-weighted seconds, extra from 2,757 GPU-seconds (every labelled PR and twice a day on main) to none; per run the nightly suites gain 1,387 registered seconds on H100, 246 on the 5090, 670 on 2×H100 (1,340 GPU-weighted) and 110 on 4×H100 (440 GPU-weighted), and 4×B200 is unchanged. What a non-LoRA PR can now break without failing its own CI, found only on the next completed nightly run: adapter lifecycle and eviction, HiCache adapter isolation, the independent MoE reference (vLLM parity), overlap loading, PD transfer, the dense breakable prefill graph, the chunked-prefill HF guard, RL tensor loading and the TP matrices.
8. **`test: retry the adapter download in test_lora_load_from_tensor on hub rate limits`** — the 5090 batch of the group rerun on this branch failed in this file's `setUpClass` on a hub 429 ("3000 api requests per 5 minutes", retry after 49 s) with no cached adapter on the runner; CI retries test methods, not `setUpClass`, and waits about two seconds. The adapter download now goes through `sglang.srt.utils.retry` (three retries, about 30, 60 and 60 s).
Rerun convention (a review rule, not path-based CI enforcement): a PR that changes `python/sglang/srt/lora`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora` or the LoRA tests runs `/rerun-group lora` before merge; a PR that changes the scheduler, the radix or HiCache caches, PD disaggregation or model LoRA integration reruns the affected LoRA tests with `/rerun-test`.

## Validation
- `/rerun-group lora` on an earlier head of this branch (c80c0a00e9): 92 members, 96 runs across 7 pools, all green. On review that run carried one failure hidden by the test framework's automatic CI retry (the TP-overlap mismatch above); read every attempt, not only job status.
- Targeted CI on 3ba65fbd8c (the same content as this head before the rebases, minus the tolerance commit): the six CPU files and the Marlin runtime unit (ubuntu), both virtual-experts files, the parallel-groups test, the Marlin shared-outer unit and the RL test (5090), the six H100 kernel files plus the routing test (H100), the MoE runner numerics (B200), vLLM parity, spec decoding, multi-LoRA, overlap loading and the Qwen3-8B trainer comparison (H100), TP, MoE TP and TP overlap loading (2×H100): all passed with no retried attempt, except the two items below. The tolerance commit then passed `test_lora_tp_overlap_loading` on 2×H100 on its first attempt.
- **Decode-graph fault, now fixed on main:** the per-PR prefill-graph file failed Guard C on H100 (both attempts) and on H200 on a production fault — the `triton_v2` + `lora_cutedsl` decode graph gave one adapter row a wrong token after graph prefills (the full-graph arm failed the same way on GB300). The guard is correct and stays as written; #46720 (merged 2026-10-30) fixed the attention-metadata lifetime across graph variants, and this head is rebased onto it. With the dual decode graph enabled in the `triton_v2` arms and the replay observer (commit 4), both prefill-graph files pass on a GB300 (SM103, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2) at this tree on their first attempt, 75 s and 128 s, so the original Blackwell failure is closed on the hardware where it reproduced; on this head the pair also passed on H100 (run 41144682705: 102 s and 155 s, no retry) and on B200 (run 41144657118: 206 s and 130 s, no retry).
- Before CI, every file that does not need gated Llama weights was run on an H200 at the exact tree (CPU units, 10 kernel files, parity, Qwen3-8B, MoE TP2, both prefill-graph files, HiCache); earlier rounds on a GB300.
- `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` over every registered test, pre-commit over every file this PR touches, and the handler's own `resolve_test_group_specs("lora")` are green at this head. This head is a rebase onto main 8ecabd3c1e and a re-split of the validated commits. Main's LoRA changes since the validated runs and how they are absorbed: #46500 rewrote `LoRADrainer` and moved its unit tests to `unit/lora/test_lora_drainer.py` — this PR's own drainer unit (written against the old API) is dropped in favour of main's file, which joins the `lora` group unchanged; #45951 (multi-LoRA under PP) added `unit/lora/test_lora_pp.py`, which joins the group unchanged, and three constructor arguments of `LoRAMemoryPool`, taken over in `test_mem_pool_ep_unit`; #46743 added a csgmv segment-grid case to `test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph`, merged as is; #46720 changed only `test_lora_inactive_batch_skip`, a group member this PR does not touch; three one-line AMD suite renames and the bot's `est_time` refresh in #46481 (the refreshed values are taken for the files whose estimates this PR does not set, and this PR's calibrated values are kept for the 17 files it re-estimated, moved or deleted). On top, a test-only simplification is folded into the four test commits (seven single-use helpers inlined, the in-place MoE fixture specialized to its one call, docstrings and comments shortened; 15 of the 22 touched files are identical to the validated content once docstrings are stripped, and the other 7 change only how a local helper is called; test cases, assertions, registrations, hardware placement, `est_time` and tolerances are unchanged). The tree was not rerun through CI as such.

- Folded into the six commits on 2026-10-30 after review: the group completion, the Marlin relocation, the dual-graph decode arms with the replay observer, the overlap-loader immediate-completion guard and the fixture simplifications. Checked per commit (compile, registered-test lint, import resolution), pre-commit on every touched file, the handler's `resolve_test_group_specs("lora")` (110 members, 114 runs, 6 pools, no error), CPU runs of the touched CPU files; the down-B kit's plans and launch config compared before and after on CPU are identical. `/rerun-group lora` on 85e8dcd0b6 (2026-10-30): 2×H100 run 41141215587, 4×B200 41141230720, 5090 41141244950 (including the relocated Marlin case), CPU 41141259062 and 4×H100 41141271618 all green; H100 run 41141200668 green on 43 of 45 files, the two prefill-graph files failing on a test-only bug in the replay observer (`sglang.Engine` is a lazy-import proxy, so the scheduler-launch override never reached the real class and the replay list stayed empty while the pass counters showed every decode step on a graph), fixed since in commit 4; the Marlin matrix (41141209927) green. The CPU suite run (41141214137) failed only on `unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py`, broken on main at that base by #47415 and fixed by #47537; this head is rebased past the fix. On d717545832 (this content before the est_time refresh): the prefill-graph pair green on H100 (41144682705) and B200 (41144657118), and the CPU suite green in every partition (41144691829). The est_time refresh and the nightly move after that are registration and comment changes only (`check_registered_tests` and the handler's group resolution pass); the rebase onto 01fde5cb62 absorbed #47603, which had removed the CI-skipped TP1-vs-TP2 case this PR had already replaced. The rebase onto b80178734d (2026-11-01) absorbed #47619, the CUDA re-tier, whose one-word stage changes conflicted in six LoRA files: this PR keeps its own stages for five of them (nightly for `test_lora_update`, `test_disaggregation_lora`, Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3-VL; per PR for the TP=2 `test_lora_tp`) and takes #47619's weekly for gpt-oss-20b; the five files this PR had moved from the 5090 to H100 return to the 5090 (`1-gpu-small`), which the nightly workflow now has, with the `est_time` they carried there (their content is what the 5090 group run 41141244950 passed, apart from one docstring; their H100 run 41242333752 at the previous head also passed). The seven commits were rebuilt from the resolved tree and checked per commit (compile, registered-test lint, import resolution); pre-commit and the handler's group resolution (110 members, 114 runs, 6 pools) pass. Main's 23 new commits touch no LoRA code but change the scheduler and both CUDA-graph runners, so `/rerun-group lora` was run on the rebased head 771658f03b (2026-11-01): H100 run 41285414398 (45 files in two partitions, 930 s and 905 s, every file on its first attempt), 2×H100 41285423494, 4×B200 41285432643, 4×H100 41285462530 and CPU 41285453071 all green; the 5090 run 41285442415 passed 12 of 13 files and errored on `rl/test_lora_load_from_tensor` before any test ran (the hub rate limit above, commit 8), after which that file passed on the 5090 at this head (run 41288518365, 2 tests, 42 s, no retry needed).

Known watch item: `test_multi_lora_backend` HF-compares the split-batch route patterns `[A,None,B]` and `[None,B,None]`, which the harness had commented out as flaky when the tolerance was exact (now ROUGE-L ≥ 0.9 on one fixed prompt). It passed in every run so far; if it flakes later, diagnose before touching the cases.

+"""Compare breakable and eager prefill for LoRA, base and mixed batches.
+
+Each backend arm builds its own eager reference. A log probe around a lone
+LoRA request requires graph replay, and the adapter must change logprobs.
+"""
+
+import os
+import re
+import shutil
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+import requests
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import kill_process_tree
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+    popen_launch_server,
+)
+
+BASE_MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B"
+LORA_ADAPTER = "nissenj/Qwen3-4B-lora-v2"
+LORA_NAME = "lora0"
+
+# Deterministic inference removes batch-composition differences. Both backends
+# measured zero diff on H200; 1e-2 leaves numerical headroom.
+GRAPH_VS_EAGER_TOLERANCE = 1e-2
+# The adapter must move at least one prompt logprob by this much.
+LORA_EFFECT_THRESHOLD = 5e-2
+
+# Prompt lengths chosen to land in different captured token buckets.
+PROMPTS = [
+    "What is the capital of France?",
+    "List three benefits of regular exercise. " * 8,
+    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 40,
+]
+
+MIXED_BATCH_PROMPTS = [
+    "Summarize the plot of Romeo and Juliet.",
+    "Explain how photosynthesis works. " * 6,
+    "Write a haiku about the sea.",
+    "Describe the water cycle in detail. " * 12,
+]
+MIXED_BATCH_LORA_PATHS = [LORA_NAME, None, LORA_NAME, None]
+
+PREFILL_GRAPH_REPLAY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"Prefill batch.*cuda graph: True")
+
+
+def _generate(text, lora_path):
+    resp = requests.post(
+        DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST + "/generate",
+        json={
+            "text": text,
+            "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 0, "temperature": 0.0},
+            "return_logprob": True,
+            "logprob_start_len": 0,
+            "lora_path": lora_path,
+        },
+        timeout=120,
+    )
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+    return resp.json()
+
+
+def _prompt_logprobs(out):
+    # First entry has no logprob (no preceding context).
+    return [logprob for logprob, _, _ in out["meta_info"]["input_token_logprobs"]][1:]
+
+
+def _max_abs_diff(a, b):
+    ta, tb = torch.tensor(a, dtype=torch.float64), torch.tensor(b, dtype=torch.float64)
+    assert ta.shape == tb.shape, f"token count mismatch: {ta.shape} vs {tb.shape}"
+    return (ta - tb).abs().max().item()
+
+
+class BCGLoRAServerMixin:
+    """Compare graph/eager servers for the subclass's ``lora_backend``."""
+
+    lora_backend: str
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _server_args(cls, prefill_backend):
+        return [
+            "--enable-lora",
+            "--lora-paths",
+            f"{LORA_NAME}={LORA_ADAPTER}",
+            "--max-loras-per-batch",
+            "2",
+            "--lora-backend",
+            cls.lora_backend,
+            "--cuda-graph-backend-prefill",
+            prefill_backend,
+            "--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill",
+            "1024",
+            "--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode",
+            "8",
+            "--disable-radix-cache",
+            "--mem-fraction-static",
+            "0.8",
+            "--random-seed",
+            "42",
+            "--enable-deterministic-inference",
+        ]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _collect(cls):
+        return {
+            "lora": [_prompt_logprobs(_generate(p, LORA_NAME)) for p in PROMPTS],
+            "base": [_prompt_logprobs(_generate(p, None)) for p in PROMPTS],
+            "mixed": [
+                _prompt_logprobs(out)
+                for out in _generate(MIXED_BATCH_PROMPTS, MIXED_BATCH_LORA_PATHS)
+            ],
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _log_sizes(cls):
+        return [os.path.getsize(path) for path in (cls.stdout_path, cls.stderr_path)]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _probe_lora_replay_window(cls):
+        """Return logs from a lone adapter request to prove LoRA-specific replay."""
+        # Pipe-dump threads flush asynchronously; drain earlier batch logs first.
+        sizes = cls._log_sizes()
+        quiet_deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
+        while time.monotonic() < quiet_deadline:
+            time.sleep(1.0)
+            new_sizes = cls._log_sizes()
+            if new_sizes == sizes:
+                break
+            sizes = new_sizes
+
+        _generate(PROMPTS[0], LORA_NAME)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
+        while True:
+            chunks = []
+            # Binary read: the size snapshot is a byte offset.
+            for path, start in zip((cls.stdout_path, cls.stderr_path), sizes):
+                with open(path, "rb") as f:
+                    f.seek(start)
+                    chunks.append(f.read().decode(errors="replace"))
+            window = "\n".join(chunks)
+            if PREFILL_GRAPH_REPLAY_PATTERN.search(window) or (
+                time.monotonic() > deadline
+            ):
+                return window
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.log_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"bcg_lora_{cls.lora_backend}_")
+        cls.stdout_path = os.path.join(cls.log_dir, "server.out")
+        cls.stderr_path = os.path.join(cls.log_dir, "server.err")
+        cls.stdout = open(cls.stdout_path, "w")
+        cls.stderr = open(cls.stderr_path, "w")
+        process = popen_launch_server(
+            BASE_MODEL,
+            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+            other_args=cls._server_args("breakable"),
+            return_stdout_stderr=(cls.stdout, cls.stderr),
+        )
+        try:
+            cls.with_graph = cls._collect()
+            cls.lora_replay_window = cls._probe_lora_replay_window()
+        finally:
+            kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+            cls.stdout.close()
+            cls.stderr.close()
+
+        process = popen_launch_server(
+            BASE_MODEL,
+            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+            other_args=cls._server_args("disabled"),
+        )
+        try:
+            cls.without_graph = cls._collect()
+        finally:
+            kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        for attr in ("stdout", "stderr"):
+            f = getattr(cls, attr, None)
+            if f is not None and not f.closed:
+                f.close()
+        log_dir = getattr(cls, "log_dir", None)
+        if log_dir:
+            shutil.rmtree(log_dir, ignore_errors=True)
+
+    def test_lora_request_replays_prefill_graph(self):
+        # PrefillCudaGraphRunner logs the marker only on graph replay; a lone
+        # LoRA request catches adapter-specific eager fallback, and without
+        # any replay the breakable-vs-eager comparison is vacuous.
+        prefill_lines = [
+            line
+            for line in self.lora_replay_window.splitlines()
+            if "Prefill batch" in line
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(
+            any(PREFILL_GRAPH_REPLAY_PATTERN.search(line) for line in prefill_lines),
+            "LoRA probe request was not served by the prefill CUDA graph. "
+            f"Prefill lines in the probe window: {prefill_lines}",
+        )
+
+    def test_lora_prefill_logprobs_match_eager(self):
+        for i, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS):
+            diff = _max_abs_diff(
+                self.with_graph["lora"][i], self.without_graph["lora"][i]
+            )
+            print(f"[lora] prompt {i} ({len(prompt)} chars): max_abs_diff={diff:.5f}")
+            self.assertLess(
+                diff,
+                GRAPH_VS_EAGER_TOLERANCE,
+                f"LoRA prompt logprobs diverge between breakable prefill graph "
+                f"and eager prefill for prompt {i}",
+            )
+
+    def test_base_prefill_logprobs_match_eager(self):
+        for i, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS):
+            diff = _max_abs_diff(
+                self.with_graph["base"][i], self.without_graph["base"][i]
+            )
+            print(f"[base] prompt {i} ({len(prompt)} chars): max_abs_diff={diff:.5f}")
+            self.assertLess(
+                diff,
+                GRAPH_VS_EAGER_TOLERANCE,
+                f"Base-model prompt logprobs diverge between breakable prefill "
+                f"graph and eager prefill for prompt {i}",
+            )
+
+    def test_mixed_batch_matches_eager(self):
+        for i in range(len(MIXED_BATCH_PROMPTS)):
+            diff = _max_abs_diff(
+                self.with_graph["mixed"][i], self.without_graph["mixed"][i]
+            )
+            print(
+                f"[mixed] req {i} (lora={MIXED_BATCH_LORA_PATHS[i]}): "
+                f"max_abs_diff={diff:.5f}"
+            )
+            self.assertLess(
+                diff,
+                GRAPH_VS_EAGER_TOLERANCE,
+                f"Mixed LoRA/base batch logprobs diverge between breakable "
+                f"prefill graph and eager prefill for request {i}",
+            )
+
+    def test_lora_is_applied_under_graph(self):
+        # Dropped LoRA kernels or stale metadata would erase this difference.
+        for i in range(len(PROMPTS)):
+            diff = _max_abs_diff(self.with_graph["lora"][i], self.with_graph["base"][i])
+            print(f"[effect] prompt {i}: lora-vs-base max_abs_diff={diff:.5f}")
+            self.assertGreater(
+                diff,
+                LORA_EFFECT_THRESHOLD,
+                f"Adapter did not change prompt logprobs under the breakable "
+                f"prefill graph for prompt {i}; LoRA was likely not applied.",
+            )

+"""Inkling sink fixtures and a reference over raw, pre-scaled MoE pool buffers."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.inkling_moe import silu_and_mul_triton  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.lora.backend.triton_v2_backend import TritonV2LoRABackend  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.models.inkling_common.lora import (  # noqa: E402
+    InklingBatchDenseMLPWithLoRAV2,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.inkling_common.util import deinterleave_gate_up  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context, get_parallel  # noqa: E402
+
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+
+DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
+
+SLOTS, RMAX = 4, 32
+
+RANKS = [32, 16, 0, 8]  # slot 2 holds no adapter
+
+HIDDEN, N_EXPERTS, F = 256, 2, 128
+
+TOL = dict(rtol=3e-2, atol=3e-2)
+
+V2 = InklingBatchDenseMLPWithLoRAV2
+
+
+def _fill_slot(bufs, slot: int, rank: int, g: torch.Generator) -> None:
+    """One slot as the pool writes it: max-rank spaced, zero tails, pre-scaled B."""
+    a_gu, b_gu, a_dn, b_dn = bufs
+    outer, f, rmax = a_gu.shape[1], b_gu.shape[2] // 2, b_gu.shape[3]
+    for buf in bufs:
+        buf[slot].zero_()
+    if rank == 0:
+        return
+
+    def rnd(*shape):
+        return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.05).to(DTYPE)
+
+    for half in range(2):
+        a_gu[slot, :, half * rmax : half * rmax + rank] = rnd(outer, rank, HIDDEN)
+    b_gu[slot, :, :, :rank] = rnd(N_EXPERTS, 2 * f, rank)
+    a_dn[slot, :, :rank] = rnd(N_EXPERTS, rank, f)
+    b_dn[slot, :, :, :rank] = rnd(outer, HIDDEN, rank)
+
+
+def _pool(shared_outer: bool, seed: int, f: int = F, ranks=RANKS, rmax: int = RMAX):
+    outer = 1 if shared_outer else N_EXPERTS
+    bufs = (
+        torch.zeros(SLOTS, outer, 2 * rmax, HIDDEN, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
+        torch.zeros(SLOTS, N_EXPERTS, 2 * f, rmax, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
+        torch.zeros(SLOTS, N_EXPERTS, rmax, f, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
+        torch.zeros(SLOTS, outer, HIDDEN, rmax, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE),
+    )
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    for slot, rank in enumerate(ranks):
+        _fill_slot(bufs, slot, rank, g)
+    return bufs
+
+
+def _swiglu_interleaved(y, gammas):
+    """Run the fused gated activation for the served interleaved layout."""
+    t, n, two_f = y.shape
+    return silu_and_mul_triton(y.reshape(t * n, two_f), gammas.reshape(-1)).view(
+        t, n, two_f // 2
+    )
+
+
+def _base_w13(w13_lin):
+    """Convert each expert to [gate | up]; reference weights stay interleaved."""
+    rows = w13_lin.shape[0] // N_EXPERTS
+    return torch.stack(
+        [deinterleave_gate_up(e, dim=0) for e in w13_lin.view(N_EXPERTS, rows, -1)]
+    ).reshape_as(w13_lin)
+
+
+def _reference(x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin, bufs, token_slots, shared_outer):
+    a_gu, b_gu, a_dn, b_dn = (b.float() for b in bufs)
+    t, n, f, rmax = x.shape[0], N_EXPERTS, b_gu.shape[2] // 2, b_gu.shape[3]
+    y = (x.float() @ w13_lin.float().T).view(t, n, 2 * f)
+    for i, s in enumerate(token_slots):
+        if s < 0:
+            continue
+        for e in range(n):
+            a = a_gu[s, 0 if shared_outer else e]  # [2R, hidden]
+            bridge = (
+                (x[i].float() @ a.T).to(DTYPE).float()
+            )  # bf16 bridge, as the kernels
+            y[i, e, 0::2] += bridge[:rmax] @ b_gu[s, e, :f].T
+            y[i, e, 1::2] += bridge[rmax:] @ b_gu[s, e, f:].T
+    act = _swiglu_interleaved(y.to(DTYPE), gammas)  # [t, n, f]
+    out = act.reshape(t, -1).float() @ w2_lin.float()
+    for i, s in enumerate(token_slots):
+        if s < 0:
+            continue
+        if shared_outer:
+            bridge = sum(act[i, e].float() @ a_dn[s, e].T for e in range(n))
+            out[i] += bridge.to(DTYPE).float() @ b_dn[s, 0].T
+        else:
+            for e in range(n):
+                bridge = (act[i, e].float() @ a_dn[s, e].T).to(DTYPE).float()
+                out[i] += bridge @ b_dn[s, e].T
+    return out
+
+
+def _batch(decode: bool, slots: list[int] | None = None, ranks=RANKS):
+    seq_lens = [1] * 13 if decode else [5, 17, 1, 9]
+    if slots is None:
+        slots = [i % SLOTS for i in range(13)] if decode else [1, 0, 2, 3]
+    fb = SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE if decode else ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+        batch_size=len(seq_lens),
+        extend_seq_lens=torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=list(seq_lens),
+        extend_num_tokens=int(sum(seq_lens)),
+        spec_info=None,
+        return_logprob=False,
+        extend_logprob_start_lens_cpu=None,
+    )
+    token_slots = [
+        slot if ranks[slot] > 0 else -1
+        for slot, length in zip(slots, seq_lens)
+        for _ in range(length)
+    ]
+    return fb, slots, token_slots
+
+
+def _inputs(t: int, f: int = F, seed: int = 11):
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(t, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
+    gammas = torch.rand(t, N_EXPERTS, generator=g, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE) + 0.5
+    w13_lin = (
+        torch.randn(N_EXPERTS * 2 * f, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.02
+    ).to(DTYPE)
+    w2_lin = (torch.randn(N_EXPERTS * f, HIDDEN, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.02).to(
+        DTYPE
+    )
+    return x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin
+
+
+def _layer(cls, backend, bufs, *, f: int = F, tp_size: int = 1, tp_rank: int = 0):
+    """The LoRA wrapper on a bare sink (no base weights to build)."""
+    layer = cls.__new__(cls)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.n_shared_experts = N_EXPERTS
+    layer.tp_group = None
+    layer.inference_moe_w13_interleaved = True
+    layer._linearized_bf16_enabled = True
+    layer._w13_gate_up_contiguous = cls is V2
+    layer.moe_tp_size, layer.moe_tp_rank = tp_size, tp_rank
+    layer.intermediate_size_per_partition = f
+    layer.initialize_lora(backend)
+    if bufs is not None:
+        layer.set_lora_info(*bufs)
+    return layer
+
+
+def _v2_backend():
+    backend = TritonV2LoRABackend(SLOTS, DEVICE)
+    backend.is_moe_lora = True
+    return backend
+
+
+SINK_PREFIX = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.shared_experts"
+
+
+def _real_sink(
+    cls, *, f: int = F, tp_size: int = 1, tp_rank: int = 0, lora_backend=None
+):
+    """Construct under the serving configuration before any weight is loaded."""
+    if lora_backend is None:
+        lora_backend = "triton_v2" if cls is V2 else "triton"
+    default = torch.get_default_dtype()
+    torch.set_default_dtype(DTYPE)
+    try:
+        # The sink partitions its shared experts over the "tp" group, which
+        # resolves to the published tp_size and the overridden tp_rank before
+        # any process group exists.
+        with (
+            get_context().override_server_args(
+                enable_lora=True, lora_backend=lora_backend, tp_size=tp_size
+            ),
+            get_parallel().override(tp_rank=tp_rank),
+        ):
+            layer = cls(
+                n_shared_experts=N_EXPERTS,
+                d_model=HIDDEN,
+                shared_d_mlp=f * tp_size,
+                layer_id=0,
+                prefix=SINK_PREFIX,
+                inference_moe_w13_interleaved=True,
+                parallel_group="tp",
+                linearized_bf16=True,
+            )
+    finally:
+        torch.set_default_dtype(default)
+    return layer.to(DEVICE)
+
+
+def _load_w13(layer, w13_lin):
+    """Load checkpoint [N, 2F, H] gate/up weights through the TP-sliced loader."""
+    full = w13_lin.view(N_EXPERTS, -1, HIDDEN)
+    layer.weight_loader_fused(
+        layer.w13_weight, full, f"{SINK_PREFIX}.w13_weight", "w13"
+    )
+
+
+def _load_w2(layer, w2_lin):
+    """Load the linearized [N*F, H] down rows as the checkpoint's [N, H, F]."""
+    full = w2_lin.view(N_EXPERTS, -1, HIDDEN).transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
+    layer.weight_loader_fused(layer.w2_weight, full, f"{SINK_PREFIX}.w2_weight", "w2")
+
+
+def _prepare(backend, fb, slots, ranks=RANKS, *, graph=False, prefill_graph=False):
+    backend.prepare_lora_batch(
+        fb,
+        slots,
+        list(ranks),
+        [1.0] * SLOTS,
+        use_decode_cuda_graph=graph,
+        use_prefill_cuda_graph=prefill_graph,
+    )
+    backend.batch_info.has_active_lora = any(
+        slot >= 0 and ranks[slot] > 0 for slot in slots
+    )
+
+
+def _forward(layer, x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin):
+    return layer._forward_bf16_linearized(
+        x, gammas, (w13_lin, w2_lin), use_reduce_scatter=True
+    )

+"""Compare MoE LoRA prefill and decode graph replay with eager.
+
+The per-PR and nightly files run independent configuration lists and eager
+references.
+The triton_v2 arms run with SGLANG_ENABLE_LORA_DUAL_GRAPH, so adapter and
+base decode batches replay both decode graph variants of one batch size.
+"""
+
+import os
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from functools import partial
+from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.engine import Engine
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.test.lora_utils import (
+    MOE_BASE_MODEL_PATH,
+    MOE_LORA_PATH,
+    MOE_LORA_TEST_PROMPTS,
+)
+
+# Missing adapters shift logprobs by 7-17.
+LOGPROB_THRESHOLD = 1.0
+MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 8
+# Keep padded buckets within the runner's 2x token-count limit.
+PREFILL_GRAPH_BATCH_SIZES = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]

+def run_moe_lora_tp_generation(
+    tp_size: int, prompts: List[str], port: int = DEFAULT_PORT_FOR_SRT_TEST_RUNNER
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Generate with the MoE adapter and settings used by the vLLM reference."""
+    with SRTRunner(
+        model_path=MOE_BASE_MODEL_PATH,
+        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        model_type="generation",
+        tp_size=tp_size,
+        lora_paths=[MOE_LORA_PATH],
+        max_loras_per_batch=1,
+        trust_remote_code=True,
+        disable_radix_cache=True,
+        port=port,
+        attention_backend="flashinfer",
+        mem_fraction_static=0.80,
+    ) as runner:
+        outputs = runner.forward(
+            prompts, max_new_tokens=10, lora_paths=[MOE_LORA_PATH] * len(prompts)
+        )
+    return {
+        "top_input_logprobs": outputs.top_input_logprobs,
+        "top_output_logprobs": outputs.top_output_logprobs,
+        "output_strs": outputs.output_strs,
+    }
+
+
+def kl_v2(a, b):
+    """Mean of 0.5 * (a - b) ** 2 over two logprob sequences of equal length."""
+    return (((a - b) ** 2) * 0.5).mean().item()
+
+
+def _single_sequence(test_case, values, name, length):
+    """Return a nonempty, finite 1-D sequence of the required length."""
+    values = torch.as_tensor(values, dtype=torch.float64)
+    if values.dim() == 2 and values.shape[0] == 1:
+        values = values[0]
+    test_case.assertEqual(values.dim(), 1, f"{name}: shape {tuple(values.shape)}")
+    test_case.assertEqual(values.numel(), length, f"{name}: positions")
+    test_case.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(values).all(), f"{name}: non-finite values")
+    return values
+
+
+def get_prompt_logprobs(engine, input_ids, lora_path):
+    """Score every token after the first in one sequence of token IDs."""
+    if isinstance(input_ids, torch.Tensor):
+        input_ids = input_ids.tolist()
+    if not isinstance(input_ids[0], list):
+        input_ids = [input_ids]
+    out = engine.generate(
+        input_ids=input_ids,
+        sampling_params={"max_new_tokens": 0, "temperature": 0.0},
+        return_logprob=True,
+        logprob_start_len=0,
+        lora_path=lora_path,
+    )
+    if isinstance(out, list):
+        out = out[0]
+    return [logprob for logprob, _, _ in out["meta_info"]["input_token_logprobs"]][1:]
+
+
+def assert_lora_matches_trainer_logprobs(
+    test_case, engine, adapter_path, kl_threshold, lora_path="my_lora"
+):
+    """Require an adapter effect and kl_v2 within `kl_threshold` of the trainer
+    logprobs in compare_sample_train_data.pt."""
+    cdata = torch.load(
+        os.path.join(adapter_path, "compare_sample_train_data.pt"),
+        weights_only=False,
+    )
+
+    # Require every position: a one-position result could broadcast against
+    # the trainer's sequence and pass.
+    tokens = torch.as_tensor(cdata["tokens"]).flatten()
+    length = tokens.numel() - 1
+    test_case.assertGreater(length, 0, "the recorded sample has one token")
+    base_t, lora_t, training, sampling = (
+        _single_sequence(test_case, values, name, length)
+        for values, name in (
+            (get_prompt_logprobs(engine, cdata["tokens"], None), "base logprobs"),
+            (get_prompt_logprobs(engine, cdata["tokens"], lora_path), "lora logprobs"),
+            (cdata["training_logprobs"], "training_logprobs"),
+            (cdata["sampling_logprobs"], "sampling_logprobs"),
+        )
+    )
+    diff = (base_t - lora_t).abs()
+    print(
+        f"[VERIFY] base vs lora: mean_diff={diff.mean().item():.6f}, "
+        f"max_diff={diff.max().item():.6f}, "
+        f"identical={torch.equal(base_t, lora_t)}"
+    )
+
+    test_case.assertFalse(
+        torch.equal(base_t, lora_t),
+        "LoRA logprobs should differ from base model logprobs",
+    )
+
+    kl_sglang_trainer = kl_v2(training, lora_t)
+    kl_orig_trainer = kl_v2(training, sampling)
+    kl_sglang_orig = kl_v2(lora_t, sampling)
+
+    print(f"KL(orig_sampler, trainer) = {kl_orig_trainer:.6e}")
+    print(f"KL(sglang, trainer)       = {kl_sglang_trainer:.6e}")
+    print(f"KL(sglang, orig_sampler)  = {kl_sglang_orig:.6e}")
+
+    test_case.assertLessEqual(
+        kl_sglang_trainer,
+        kl_threshold,
+        f"KL(sglang, trainer) = {kl_sglang_trainer:.6e} exceeds "
+        f"threshold {kl_threshold}",
+    )

+"""Nightly Inkling sink executor, tail-width, layout and TP-shard matrix.
+Core replay and reload guards live in test_dense_lora_inkling_sink.py.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("triton")
+
+from sglang.srt.lora.dense.plan import (  # noqa: E402
+    AFamily,
+    BFamily,
+    DensePlan,
+    Overlap,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.inkling_common.dense_mlp import (  # noqa: E402
+    InklingBatchDenseMLP,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.inkling_common.util import deinterleave_gate_up  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.test.kits.inkling_sink_lora_kit import (
+    DEVICE,
+    DTYPE,
+    HIDDEN,
+    N_EXPERTS,
+    RANKS,
+    RMAX,
+    SLOTS,
+    TOL,
+    V2,
+    _base_w13,
+    _batch,
+    _forward,
+    _inputs,
+    _layer,
+    _load_w2,
+    _load_w13,
+    _pool,
+    _prepare,
+    _real_sink,
+    _reference,
+    _v2_backend,
+)
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="nightly", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="the sink kernels need CUDA"
+)
+
+# A pool rank whose shared gate/up bridge (2R = 32 columns) is narrower than
+# the shrink's 64-wide column tile.
+SMALL_RMAX, SMALL_RANKS = 16, [16, 8, 0, 8]
+
+
+def _tiles(**overrides):
+    tiles = dict(DensePlan().a_tiles)
+    tiles.update(overrides)
+    return tiles
+
+
+# Overlap.AB_DELTA is site-agnostic apply() plumbing; test_dense_lora_kernels covers it.
+PLANS = {
+    "grouped": DensePlan(),
+    "grouped_sorted_splitk_serial": DensePlan(a_tiles=_tiles(SPLIT_K=4)),
+    "grouped_splitk_planes": DensePlan(a_tiles=_tiles(SPLIT_K=2, SPLIT_MODE="planes")),
+    "grouped_overlap_a": DensePlan(overlap=Overlap.A),
+    "per_row_a_grouped_b": DensePlan(a_family=AFamily.PER_ROW, overlap=Overlap.A),
+    "per_row": DensePlan(
+        a_family=AFamily.PER_ROW, b_family=BFamily.PER_ROW, overlap=Overlap.A
+    ),
+    "all_slots": DensePlan(a_family=AFamily.ALL_SLOTS, b_family=BFamily.PER_ROW),
+    "all_slots_overlap_a": DensePlan(
+        a_family=AFamily.ALL_SLOTS, b_family=BFamily.PER_ROW, overlap=Overlap.A
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def _pin_plan(backend, plan: DensePlan) -> None:
+    backend.runner.plan_for = (
+        lambda kind, max_rank, in_features=0, out_features=0, *, num_tokens: plan
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shared_outer,decode,rmax",
+    [(shared, decode, RMAX) for shared in (True, False) for decode in (True, False)]
+    + [(True, False, SMALL_RMAX)],
+)
+def test_v2_tail_width_matches_reference(shared_outer, decode, rmax):
+    f = 96
+    ranks = RANKS if rmax == RMAX else SMALL_RANKS
+    bufs = _pool(shared_outer, seed=3 + shared_outer, f=f, ranks=ranks, rmax=rmax)
+    fb, slots, token_slots = _batch(decode, ranks=ranks)
+    x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin = _inputs(fb.extend_num_tokens, f=f)
+    backend = _v2_backend()
+    _prepare(backend, fb, slots, ranks)
+    layer = _layer(V2, backend, bufs, f=f)
+    out = _forward(layer, x, gammas, _base_w13(w13_lin), w2_lin)
+    expected = _reference(x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin, bufs, token_slots, shared_outer)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, **TOL)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shared_outer,plan_name,decode,rmax",
+    [
+        (shared, name, decode, RMAX)
+        for shared in (True, False)
+        for name in sorted(PLANS)
+        if shared or not name.startswith("all_slots")
+        for decode in (True, False)
+    ]
+    + [(shared, "grouped", False, SMALL_RMAX) for shared in (True, False)],
+)
+def test_v2_every_executor_family(shared_outer, plan_name, decode, rmax):
+    """Exercise every sink executor with full and partial shrink tiles."""
+    ranks = RANKS if rmax == RMAX else SMALL_RANKS
+    bufs = _pool(shared_outer, seed=5, ranks=ranks, rmax=rmax)
+    fb, slots, token_slots = _batch(decode, ranks=ranks)
+    x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin = _inputs(fb.extend_num_tokens)
+    backend = _v2_backend()
+    _prepare(backend, fb, slots, ranks)
+    _pin_plan(backend, PLANS[plan_name])
+    layer = _layer(V2, backend, bufs)
+    out = _forward(layer, x, gammas, _base_w13(w13_lin), w2_lin)
+    expected = _reference(x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin, bufs, token_slots, shared_outer)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, **TOL)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shared_outer", [True, False], ids=["shared", "per_expert"])
+def test_v2_tp4_local_shards_sum_to_the_unsharded_output(shared_outer):
+    """Sum four TP-local base/pool shards, sliced by the wrapper on one GPU."""
+    tp, f_full = 4, 256
+    f_local = f_full // tp
+    bufs = _pool(shared_outer, seed=13, f=f_full)
+    fb, slots, token_slots = _batch(False)
+    x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin = _inputs(fb.extend_num_tokens, f=f_full)
+    backend = _v2_backend()
+    _prepare(backend, fb, slots)
+    full = _layer(V2, backend, bufs, f=f_full)
+    expected = _reference(x, gammas, w13_lin, w2_lin, bufs, token_slots, shared_outer)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        _forward(full, x, gammas, _base_w13(w13_lin), w2_lin).float(),
+        expected,
+        **TOL,
+    )
+
+    a_gu, b_gu, a_dn, b_dn = bufs
+    total = torch.zeros_like(expected)
+    for rank in range(tp):
+        layer = _layer(V2, backend, None, f=f_local, tp_size=tp, tp_rank=rank)
+        b_gu_r = torch.stack(
+            [
+                layer.slice_moe_lora_b_weights(b_gu[s], rank, "gate_up_proj_moe")
+                for s in range(SLOTS)
+            ]
+        )
+        a_dn_r = torch.stack(
+            [
+                layer.slice_moe_lora_a_weights(a_dn[s], rank, "down_proj_moe")
+                for s in range(SLOTS)
+            ]
+        )
+        assert b_gu_r.shape == (SLOTS, N_EXPERTS, 2 * f_local, RMAX)
+        assert a_dn_r.shape == (SLOTS, N_EXPERTS, RMAX, f_local)
+        layer.set_lora_info(a_gu, b_gu_r, a_dn_r, b_dn)
+        # Interleaved gate/up rows of this rank's features, and its w2 rows.
+        w13_r = (
+            w13_lin.view(N_EXPERTS, 2 * f_full, HIDDEN)[
+                :, 2 * rank * f_local : 2 * (rank + 1) * f_local
+            ]
+            .reshape(-1, HIDDEN)
+            .contiguous()
+        )
+        w2_r = (
+            w2_lin.view(N_EXPERTS, f_full, HIDDEN)[
+                :, rank * f_local : (rank + 1) * f_local
+            ]
+            .reshape(-1, HIDDEN)
+            .contiguous()
+        )
+        # The layout conversion follows the shard, as it does on the loaded rows.
+        total += _forward(layer, x, gammas, _base_w13(w13_r), w2_r).float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(total, expected, **TOL)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_rank", [0, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lora_backend", ["triton_v2", "triton"], ids=["v2", "legacy"])
+def test_w13_initial_load_and_reload_use_the_tp_local_layout(tp_rank, lora_backend):
+    tp, f_full = 4, 256
+    f_local = f_full // tp
+    sink = _real_sink(
+        InklingBatchDenseMLP,
+        f=f_local,
+        tp_size=tp,
+        tp_rank=tp_rank,
+        lora_backend=lora_backend,
+    )
+    contiguous = lora_backend == "triton_v2"
+    assert sink._w13_gate_up_contiguous is contiguous
+    _, _, w13_lin, w2_lin = _inputs(4, f=f_full)
+    pointer = sink.w13_weight.data_ptr()
+
+    def rank_rows(w13):
+        rows = w13.view(N_EXPERTS, 2 * f_full, HIDDEN)[
+            :, 2 * tp_rank * f_local : 2 * (tp_rank + 1) * f_local
+        ]
+        return (
+            torch.stack([deinterleave_gate_up(e, dim=0) for e in rows])
+            if contiguous
+            else rows
+        )
+
+    def load_and_check(w13):
+        original = w13.clone()
+        _load_w13(sink, w13)
+        assert torch.equal(w13, original)
+        assert torch.equal(sink.w13_weight.data, rank_rows(w13))
+        assert sink.w13_weight.data_ptr() == pointer
+
+    load_and_check(w13_lin)
+    _load_w2(sink, w2_lin)
+    sink.process_weights_after_loading()
+    assert torch.equal(sink.w13_weight.data, rank_rows(w13_lin))
+    lin = sink._w2_lin.clone()
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(41)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        w13_new = (torch.randn(w13_lin.shape, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.02).to(
+            DTYPE
+        )
+        load_and_check(w13_new)
+        sink.process_weights_after_loading()
+        rows, _ = sink.get_bf16_linearized_weights()
+        assert torch.equal(rows, rank_rows(w13_new).reshape_as(rows))
+        assert rows.data_ptr() == pointer
+        assert torch.equal(sink._w2_lin, lin) and sink._bf16_linearized_ready
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
